summary.headline: GPIL Q1 FY27: EBITDA margin 19.1%, PAT margin 12.7%, both flat YoY but softer QoQ on costlier merchant iron ore and imported coal.
summary.overview: Revenue grew both YoY and QoQ on higher volumes and better realisations, while EBITDA and PAT were broadly flat YoY and down sequentially on input costs. Iron ore mining volume fell because dumping space was constrained by pending tree-cutting approval on additional land, forcing market ore purchases for pellets. One of the new 2 mtpa pellet plants was shut from around mid-June/July on gas price and iron ore economics, with Q2 pellet output guided to roughly 500 kt. Management shelved the 1 mtpa integrated steel project over water allocation delays and moved the 0.7 mtpa CRM complex to Maharashtra, with commissioning now targeted December 2027.

segments.name: Iron ore mining (Ari Dongri)
segments.commentary: Mining volume declined YoY and QoQ, constrained by overburden dumping space pending government land approval. Captive mining guidance of 3.4 mt for FY27 is said to be unchanged; management expects mining cost to fall below INR2,700/t from FY28 vs INR3,000-3,500/t now.

segments.name: Pellets (4.7 mtpa expanded capacity)
segments.commentary: Ran at 77% utilisation in Q1 with all three plants operating, and pellet sales jumped in Q1 as surplus pellets went to the merchant market. One 2 mtpa plant has been shut since about mid-2026; FY27 pellet guidance of 4.0 mt is under review and expected to be lower.

segments.name: Sponge iron, billet, rolled products (value-added)
segments.commentary: Management cited healthy YoY growth in value-added production led by sponge iron, billets and rolled products. No segment volumes or revenues were given on the call.

segments.name: Galvanized products
segments.commentary: Volumes declined YoY, attributed to monsoon-season delays in project deliveries. Management described this as seasonal.

segments.name: BESS (battery energy storage, Maharashtra)
segments.commentary: About INR500 crore spent. Machine delivery starts December 2026 and first container is targeted for Q1 FY28. Containers are being quoted from August 2026.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume guidance is said to be on track, with Q1 at 16-29% of full-year guidance. Management said FY27 pellet output will be slightly lower, and a revised figure will come later.

Q2 FY27 pellet production is expected at about 500 kt if the plant stays shut for the whole quarter. Q3 is expected at full pellet capacity, with merchant ore purchases at 25-30%, falling below 10% in Q4 and to zero (fully captive) in FY28.

Mining ramp-up is expected from Q3 FY27 once government land approval comes through (targeted end-September), reaching full capacity by end Q4 FY27 or early Q1 FY28. Beneficiation plant commissioning is expected by Q3 FY27.

Margin improvement is expected from Q4 FY27 once the beneficiation plant enables higher captive pellet use. Management said CRM incentives can add 2-3% to CRM margins, taking them to 10-11% from the earlier 7-8%.
Vision 2030 target (4x revenue, 3x EBITDA and PAT) was restated without the steel plant. Management said the steel plant is on hold and no timeline is set.
capex_capacity: CRM complex (0.7 mtpa, relocated to Maharashtra near Sambhajinagar): capex raised to INR1,100 crore from earlier INR900-950 crore, including working capital margin money; INR80 crore spent so far; land about INR50 crore for 35 acres; construction from October 2026; commissioning December 2027; funded by INR550 crore debt and internal accruals. Land allotment approval is expected by end-August 2026.
BESS (20 GW... as stated in transcript, battery storage project in Maharashtra): about INR500 crore spent; remaining INR700-800 crore to be spent over FY27 and FY28; commissioning targeted Q1 FY28.
Mining and other capex: about INR2,000 crore for the remaining FY27 and the whole of FY28. No FY29 projection has been given.
Ari Dongri beneficiation plant: INR218 crore spent till June 2026; ramp-up from Q3 FY27 and full-scale operation from FY28.

Captive solar: 25 MW commissioned in May 2026; 100 MW under construction, targeted September 2026; 150 MW project in abeyance. Solar storage of 45 MW targeted for Q3 FY27 (management corrected 'Q3 27' to 'Q3 26' and then said Q3 FY27 was intended). Captive solar would reach 290 MW.
Boria Tibbu mine (0.7 mtpa now) expansion to 4 mtpa targeted for FY31, with a 4 mtpa beneficiation plant yielding 1.5-2 mt concentrate (about 40% yield). TOFR filing pending.
demand_pricing: Iron ore prices (global) expected to hover around USD90-100/t; management said it does not expect prices to fall below USD90 soon. Domestic ex-mine iron ore about INR5,500/t.
Pellet prices: ex-Raipur about INR10,000/t now, versus a July low of about INR8,700-9,000/t. Management expects long-term range INR9,000-10,000/t.
Pellet exports: two vessels exported in June-July at about INR9,000/t ex-plant, roughly at par with domestic. Exports have now stopped due to the plant shutdown.
Industry pellet utilisation is about 65%, held back by lower exports, limited high-grade supply and margin pressure. Indian pellet production was about 120 mt in FY26, up from 109 mt in FY25.
Cost: iron ore accounts for about 75% of the raw material cost increase and imported coal for about 25%. Q2 FY27 costs are expected to stay high.
Sensitivity: each INR100/t fall in pellet price reduces annual EBITDA by about INR40 crore on 4 mt of pellets (per management).
